newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian navy picks up five fleeing Albanian port.
newsitem.headline: Italian navy picks up five fleeing Albanian port.

text.p: Two adults and three children were rescued from a small boat by an Italian frigate in the Adriatic on Wednesday after they fled the troubled southern Albanian port of Vlore, coastguards said.

A spokesman for the coastguard's office in Bari, southern Italy, said the adults were Albanian and the children Italian. One adult, a woman, was "in poor condition" and was being taken by helicopter to hospital in Brindisi.
The spokesman said the other four passengers were being taken to the port of Otranto and were well. He did not know the relationship between them.
The five were picked up outside Albanian waters by the frigate Espero.
Albania has imposed a state of emergency to try to quell violence which has erupted since the collapse of dubious get-rich-quick investment schemes in Europe's poorest state.
Albanian army and police forces pushed towards the south on Wednesday to quash an armed rebellion. More than 20 people have been reported killed since Friday in Vlore.

Italian coastguards have beefed up security against a potential influx of illegal immigrants trying to make the short trip to Italy to escape the unrest. Italy is already a magnet for many illegal immigrants from across the Adriatic.
